facts.text: The node declares robot_ip_address, robot_type, trajectory_duration, robot_node_name (default dobot_bringup_ros2) and robot_number (default 1) as ROS parameters.
When robotNumber > 1 the node assigns kRobotName = robotNodeName + '/'.
The node names the EnableRobot service '/dobot_bringup_ros2/srv/EnableRobot'.
The node names the Stop service '/dobot_bringup_ros2/srv/Stop'.
The node names the MovJ service '/dobot_bringup_ros2/srv/MovJ'.
The node names the MovL service '/dobot_bringup_ros2/srv/MovL'.
The node registers the MovJ service with the generated type dobot_msgs_v4::srv::MovJ.
The EnableRobot request formatter returns the dashboard text EnableRobot().
The Stop request formatter returns the dashboard text Stop().
The MovJ parser formats a..f with three decimals, sends joint={...} when mode is true and pose={...} when it is false, and appends any non-empty param_value strings.
The MovL parser uses the same mode switch and formatting as MovJ.
MovJ is a queue command: the controller answers ErrorID,{ResultID},MovJ(...); and ResultID is the algorithm queue id.
MovL is a queue command: the controller answers ErrorID,{ResultID},MovL(...); and ResultID is the algorithm queue id.
Stop() is documented to stop motion (or a script); it can stop jogging, script execution, joint motion and a series of motions.
EnableRobot() enables the robot.
A dashboard reply has the form ErrorID,{...},Command(...); the error id is the number before the first brace.
The reply parser stores the integer before the first '{' in res and, for a _f command, the first brace-delimited payload in robot_return.
The dashboard command loop reads until it sees ';', passes timeout=0 to tcpRecv and calls sleep(0.01) on a false return; it has no overall deadline of its own.
TcpClient::tcpRecv returns false when select returns zero (no ready descriptor); when select is positive it proceeds to read.
doTcpCmd catches TcpClientException and logs the error without assigning err_id in the catch block.
callRosService calls doTcpCmd and then returns true.
The Stop callback passes response->res to callRosService.
The node opens a dashboard TcpClient to port 29999 and a feedback TcpClient to port 30004.
The README states the robot control port is 29999 and the feedback port is 30004.
The node publishes sensor_msgs/msg/JointState on the relative topic 'joint_states'.
The JointState message carries six positions copied from getJointState.
When the feedback connection is down the node copies the last valid joint positions, or zeros before any valid data.
The node publishes dobot_msgs_v4/msg/ToolVectorActual on the relative topic dobot_msgs_v4/msg/ToolVectorActual.
The ToolVectorActual publisher fills x, y, z, rx, ry, rz from getToolVectorActual and publishes only while connected.
The node creates a dobot_msgs_v4/msg/RobotStatus publisher on the relative topic dobot_msgs_v4/msg/RobotStatus.
The RobotStatus publisher fills is_enable and is_connected from the node's connection state.
isEnable() returns robot_mode == 5; isConnected() returns the dashboard TCP connect state && the feedback TCP connect state.
The publisher rate is the JointStatePublishRate ROS parameter, default 10 Hz.
The MovJ service request has bool mode, float64 a..f and string[] param_value; the response has string robot_return and int32 res.
The MovL service request has the same fields as MovJ and the same response.
The Stop service has an empty request and returns int32 res.
The EnableRobot service has an empty request and returns int32 res.
ToolVectorActual declares float64 x, y, z, rx, ry, rz.
RobotStatus declares bool is_enable and bool is_connected.
The README lists the supported models as CR3, CR5, CR7, CR10, CR12, CR16, CR20, CR30H, CR10AF, E6/ME6, Nova2 and Nova5.
The README instructs the user to ensure the robot is in a safe position, that ports 29999 and 30004 are free, and that the robot is in remote TCP/IP control mode.

safe_state.description: Unconfirmed: no native e-stop is bound because the upstream Stop response can retain res=0 after a failed TCP exchange. The latch blocks new MHS commands but neither sends a dashboard Stop nor establishes a stopped arm; motion already running may continue. The ordinary Stop service and an explicit latch reset confirm no hardware state. A reviewed stop/confirmation path and independent physical stop are required outside this blocked package.
